title: The Tiv put under the Jukun, and a Sarkin Makurdi
text: The British split the Tiv into three and kept them under outside rulers: the Jukun minority in the north-east, Cross River in the south and Lafia Division in the north-west. They went as far as appointing Audu Dan Afoba as Sarkin Makurdi, “king of Makurdi”. These arrangements failed, and in 1946 the Tiv chose their own Tor Tiv.
note: The years of the arrangement are approximate; the sources give the period, not dates.
